items.q: What is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(1)</annotation></semantics></math>?

For how many values of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> in the domain is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>?
What is the range of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>?

What is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(g(4))</annotation></semantics></math>?

Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = x^2 + 1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x) = 2x - 3</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(g(x))</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(f(x)) = 2(x^2 + 1) - 3</annotation></semantics></math>. In <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(g(x))</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> acts first: put <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x - 3</annotation></semantics></math> into <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2x - 3)^2</annotation></semantics></math> is not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4x^2 + 9</annotation></semantics></math>. Square the whole binomial: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2x - 3)^2 = 4x^2 - 12x + 9</annotation></semantics></math>.

Replace every <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> by the whole expression <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2x - 3)</annotation></semantics></math>, with parentheses: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(g(x)) = (2x - 3)^2 + 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find an equation of the line through <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-1, 5)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(3, -3)</annotation></semantics></math>. Write <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> in terms of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The slope is rise over run: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{-3 - 5}{3 - (-1)} = \frac{-8}{4} = -2</annotation></semantics></math>, not run over rise.

Check the sign of the slope: from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-1, 5)</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(3, -3)</annotation></semantics></math> the line goes down, so the slope is negative, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: What is the domain of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(x) = \frac{\sqrt{x + 4}}{x - 1}</annotation></semantics></math>?

The graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = |x|</annotation></semantics></math> is moved 3 units left and 2 units down. Which equation describes the new graph?

Which lines are the vertical and horizontal asymptotes of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(x) = \frac{2x + 1}{x - 4}</annotation></semantics></math>?

Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="true">{</mo><mtable columnalign="left left" columnspacing="1em"><mtr><mtd><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mtd><mtd><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mtd><mtd><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = \begin{cases} x^2 & x < 2 \\ 3x - 1 & x \ge 2 \end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math>. What is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(2) + f(-1)</annotation></semantics></math>?

Find the slope of the line through the points of the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = x^2 - 3x</annotation></semantics></math> where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Slope is rise over run: change in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> divided by change in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{4 - (-2)}{4 - 1} = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

Subtract in the same order on top and bottom: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{f(4) - f(1)}{4 - 1}</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{f(1) - f(4)}{4 - 1}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is the rise only. Divide by the run, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4 - 1 = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: The function <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(x) = (x^2 + 5)^3</annotation></semantics></math> can be written as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(x) = f(g(x))</annotation></semantics></math>. Which choice of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> works?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = x^3</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x) = x^2 + 5</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = x^2 + 5</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x) = x^3</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = x^3 + 5</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x) = x^2</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = 3x</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x) = x^2 + 5</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Which expression equals <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3}{x^2}</annotation></semantics></math> written as a power of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>?

Which expression equals <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}</annotation></semantics></math>?

Evaluate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>8</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8^{2/3}</annotation></semantics></math> exactly.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>8</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8^{2/3}</annotation></semantics></math> is not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8 \cdot \frac{2}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>. The denominator 3 means a cube root, the numerator 2 a square: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mroot><mn>8</mn><mn>3</mn></mroot><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\sqrt[3]{8})^2 = 2^2 = 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is only the cube root, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>8</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8^{1/3}</annotation></semantics></math>. Square it as well: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^2 = 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>8</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8^{2/3}</annotation></semantics></math> means take the cube root, then square: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mroot><mn>8</mn><mn>3</mn></mroot><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\sqrt[3]{8})^2 = 4</annotation></semantics></math>. It is not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mn>8</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{8^2}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Evaluate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>16</mn><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16^{-3/4}</annotation></semantics></math> exactly.

mistakes.why: A negative exponent means a reciprocal, not a negative number: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>16</mn><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mn>16</mn><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16^{-3/4} = \frac{1}{16^{3/4}} = \frac{1}{8}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>16</mn><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16^{3/4} = 8</annotation></semantics></math>, but the exponent is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{3}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>: take the reciprocal, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{8}</annotation></semantics></math>.

An exponent is not a multiplier. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>16</mn><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mroot><mn>16</mn><mn>4</mn></mroot><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16^{-3/4} = \frac{1}{(\sqrt[4]{16})^3} = \frac{1}{2^3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Simplify <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{(x^3)^2 \cdot x^{-4}}{x}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

Which expression equals <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x^2 + 1}{\sqrt{x}}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 0</annotation></semantics></math>, written as a sum of powers of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>?

Which expression is NOT equal to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{(2x)^3}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math>?

Which expression equals <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{1/2} \cdot x^{1/3}</annotation></semantics></math>?

Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = 6x^{-1/2} + x^{3/2}</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(4)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6x^{-1/2}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>6</mn><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{6}{\sqrt{x}}</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>6</mn><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-6\sqrt{x}</annotation></semantics></math>. A negative exponent means a reciprocal.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{3/2}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\sqrt{x})^3 = 8</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 4</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x^3}{2} = 32</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Simplify <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(2x^{-1}\right)^{-2}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

Which expression equals <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x + 3)^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ne -3</annotation></semantics></math>?

Evaluate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>27</mn><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">27^{-1/3} + 4^{1/2}</annotation></semantics></math> exactly.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>27</mn><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">27^{-1/3}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, a reciprocal, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-3</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>27</mn><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mn>27</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">27^{-1/3} = \frac{1}{27^{1/3}} = \frac{1}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, not 3. The negative exponent flips it.

items.q: Which is the factored form of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x^2 + 5x - 3</annotation></semantics></math>?

Which is the factored form of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>27</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^3 - 27</annotation></semantics></math>?

Simplify <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x^2 - 16}{x^2 + 2x - 8}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ne -4</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ne 2</annotation></semantics></math>.
Which fraction can be simplified by canceling a common factor?

What is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\sqrt{x + 5} - 3\right)\left(\sqrt{x + 5} + 3\right)</annotation></semantics></math>?

For <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ne 4</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\sqrt{x + 5} - 3}{x - 4} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{x + 5} + 3}</annotation></semantics></math>. Evaluate the simplified form at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 4</annotation></semantics></math>. This number is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to 4} \frac{\sqrt{x + 5} - 3}{x - 4}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The bottom is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mn>9</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{9} + 3 = 6</annotation></semantics></math>; the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+3</annotation></semantics></math> was dropped.

The simplified form is one over <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{x + 5} + 3</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>, not 6.

items.q: Simplify the complex fraction <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\frac{1}{x + 2} - \frac{1}{2}}{x}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ne -2</annotation></semantics></math>.

Using the simplified form <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{-1}{2(x + 2)}</annotation></semantics></math> of the complex fraction above, find its value at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Keep the sign: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{-1}{2(0 + 2)} = -\frac{1}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The denominator is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2(0 + 2) = 4</annotation></semantics></math>, not 2.

items.q: Simplify <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mi>h</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{(3 + h)^2 - 9}{h}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

A student simplifies: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x^2 - 4x}{x^2 - 16} = \frac{-4x}{-16} = \frac{x}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>. What went wrong?
options: The <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2</annotation></semantics></math> terms were canceled, but only factors can cancel; correctly, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x(x - 4)}{(x - 4)(x + 4)} = \frac{x}{x + 4}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The student should have canceled <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> instead: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x - 4}{x - 16}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The negatives should not cancel, so the answer is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{x}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: For <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ne 1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x^3 - 1}{x - 1} = x^2 + x + 1</annotation></semantics></math>. Evaluate the simplified form at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The original fraction has a zero top and bottom at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math>; that is why you simplify first. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1^2 + 1 + 1 = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^3 - 1 = (x - 1)(x^2 + x + 1)</annotation></semantics></math>, so the simplified form is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 + x + 1</annotation></semantics></math>, which is 3 at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> exactly.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> is in the second quadrant, where cosine (the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-coordinate) is negative.

The reference angle is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>; <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> is its sine.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>7</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\left(\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> exactly.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>7</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{7\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math> is just past <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, in the third quadrant, where sine (the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>-coordinate) is negative.

The reference angle is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>, whose sine is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> exactly.

mistakes.why: At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>, sine is positive and cosine is negative, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan = \frac{\sin}{\cos}</annotation></semantics></math> is negative.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> exactly.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>. Secant is its reciprocal: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}/2} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}/2} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}</annotation></semantics></math>, which simplifies to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, not 2.

items.q: What is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>135</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">135^{\circ}</annotation></semantics></math> in radians?

Which values of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 2\pi)</annotation></semantics></math> solve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\sin x = -\sqrt{3}</annotation></semantics></math>?

Which expression equals <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 - \cos^2 x</annotation></semantics></math> for every <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\sin^2 x</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: What does <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin^2 x</annotation></semantics></math> mean?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin(\sin x)</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Which expression equals <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin(2x)</annotation></semantics></math> for every <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>?

On the interval <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 < x < \pi</annotation></semantics></math>, where does the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \cos x</annotation></semantics></math> cross the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-axis?
options: It does not cross the axis there.

items.q: Use a calculator to find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos(1)</annotation></semantics></math>, where the angle is in radians. Give your answer to three decimal places.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>1</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos(1^{\circ})</annotation></semantics></math>: the calculator is in degree mode. Calculus always uses radians; switch the mode and recompute.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin(1)</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos(1)</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: For which value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan x</annotation></semantics></math> not defined?

An angle <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> is in the second quadrant and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math> exactly.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">±</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\theta = \pm\frac{4}{5}</annotation></semantics></math>; in the second quadrant cosine is negative.

Use squares: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>25</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>16</mn><mn>25</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos^2\theta = 1 - \frac{9}{25} = \frac{16}{25}</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 - \frac{3}{5}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Evaluate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{3\ln 2}</annotation></semantics></math> exactly.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\ln 2 = \ln(2^3)</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{3\ln 2} = e^{\ln 8} = 8</annotation></semantics></math>; the 3 is an exponent on 2, not a multiplier.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>e</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln</annotation></semantics></math> cancel only when <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln</annotation></semantics></math> is the whole exponent. Move the 3 inside first: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{\ln 8} = 8</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: For <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y > 0</annotation></semantics></math>, which expression equals <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln\left(\frac{x^3}{y}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\ln x)^3 - \ln y</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Solve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{2x} = 9</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>. Give the exact value.

mistakes.why: Taking <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x = \ln 9</annotation></semantics></math>; divide by 2: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \frac{\ln 9}{2} = \ln 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

Undo <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>e</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln</annotation></semantics></math>, not by dividing: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x = \ln 9</annotation></semantics></math>.

Take the log first, then divide: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \frac{\ln 9}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln\frac{9}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Solve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln(x + 2) = 1</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>. Give the exact value.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x + 2 = e</annotation></semantics></math>, so subtract 2: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = e - 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln(x + 2) = 1</annotation></semantics></math> means <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>1</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x + 2 = e^1</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x + 2 = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: What is the domain of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = \ln(4 - x)</annotation></semantics></math>?

Which expression equals <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln 12</annotation></semantics></math>?

Which describes the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = e^{-x}</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: It passes through <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0, 1)</annotation></semantics></math>, stays above the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-axis, and falls from left to right.

It passes through <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0, 1)</annotation></semantics></math> and rises from left to right.

It passes through <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0, -1)</annotation></semantics></math> and stays below the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-axis.

It passes through <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1, 0)</annotation></semantics></math> and falls from left to right.

items.q: A town's population is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>500</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>0.04</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(t) = 500e^{0.04t}</annotation></semantics></math> people, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> years from now. Use a calculator to find when the population reaches 800. Give <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> to three decimal places, with units.

mistakes.why: Divide by 500 before taking the log: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>0.04</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{0.04t} = 1.6</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1.6</mn></mrow><mn>0.04</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = \frac{\ln 1.6}{0.04}</annotation></semantics></math>.

Divide by 500 instead of subtracting it: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>500</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>0.04</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>800</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">500e^{0.04t} = 800</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>0.04</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>800</mn><mn>500</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{0.04t} = \frac{800}{500}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: For <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 0</annotation></semantics></math>, which expression equals <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln(x^2)</annotation></semantics></math>?

Evaluate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{\ln 5 + \ln 2}</annotation></semantics></math> exactly.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln 5 + \ln 2 = \ln(5 \cdot 2)</annotation></semantics></math>: a sum of logs is the log of a product, so the result is 10.

items.q: For <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 0</annotation></semantics></math>, which expression equals <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{-\ln x}</annotation></semantics></math>?

Which equation is true for every <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y > 0</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln(xy) = \ln x + \ln y</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln(x + y) = \ln x + \ln y</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\ln x}{\ln y} = \ln(x - y)</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\ln x)^2 = 2\ln x</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: A substance decays so that <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>80</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A(t) = 80e^{kt}</annotation></semantics></math> grams after <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> hours, and half of it remains after 5 hours. What is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>?

Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{-1}(9)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> is the inverse function, not a reciprocal. Find the input whose output is 9.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(4)</annotation></semantics></math>. Read the table backward: which <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = 9</annotation></semantics></math>?

items.q: The average rate of change of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[2, 3]</annotation></semantics></math> is 3. Find the average rate of change of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[6, 9]</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Swapping inputs and outputs swaps rise and run: the rate of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3 - 2}{9 - 6}</annotation></semantics></math>, the reciprocal.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> of an increasing function is increasing, so its rate is positive.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{-1}(5) + f(0)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{-1}(5)</annotation></semantics></math> is the input with output 5, which is 1, not 5.

6 is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 + 5</annotation></semantics></math>: the 5 is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(1)</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(0)</annotation></semantics></math>. Read <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(0) = 3</annotation></semantics></math> from the table; with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{-1}(5) = 1</annotation></semantics></math> the sum is 4.

items.q: Which statement about <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is true?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{-1}(3) = f(3) = 9</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{-1}(3)</annotation></semantics></math> is not defined.

items.q: Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = \frac{2x + 1}{x - 3}</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{-1}(x)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{f(x)}</annotation></semantics></math>, the reciprocal. To invert, swap <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> and solve for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>.

Check the signs when you collect terms: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(y - 3) = 2y + 1</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(x - 2) = 3x + 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: The function <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = x^3 + 2</annotation></semantics></math> is one-to-one. Write a formula for its inverse function, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{-1}(x)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Undo the steps in reverse order: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> cubes, then adds 2, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> subtracts 2, then takes the cube root.

That is the reciprocal <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{f(x)}</annotation></semantics></math>, not the inverse.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>arcsin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\arcsin\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> exactly.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\frac{2\pi}{3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> too, but arcsine only returns angles in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">[</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>; the angle whose sine is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>arccos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\arccos\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> exactly.

mistakes.why: Arccosine returns angles in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, \pi]</annotation></semantics></math>, never negative ones. Cosine is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> in quadrant II at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\frac{\pi}{3} = +\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. For <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, go to quadrant II.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>arctan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\arctan(-1)</annotation></semantics></math> exactly.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan\frac{3\pi}{4} = -1</annotation></semantics></math>, but arctangent returns angles in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>arcsin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\arcsin\left(\sin\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> exactly.

mistakes.why: Arcsine only returns angles in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">[</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{5\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math> is outside. Work inside out: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\frac{5\pi}{6} = \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Why does <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = x^2</annotation></semantics></math> need a restricted domain, such as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ge 0</annotation></semantics></math>, before it has an inverse?
options: Two inputs give the same output, as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(2) = f(-2) = 4</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is not one-to-one.
