<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2</annotation></semantics></math> has no negative outputs, so it has no inverse.
The graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2</annotation></semantics></math> is not a straight line.

items.q: The point <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, 7)</annotation></semantics></math> is on the graph of a one-to-one function <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math>, and the slope of the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> there is 4. Which is true about the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: It passes through <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(7, 2)</annotation></semantics></math>, with slope <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{4}</annotation></semantics></math> there.

It passes through <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(7, 2)</annotation></semantics></math>, with slope 4 there.

It passes through <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, 7)</annotation></semantics></math>, with slope <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{4}</annotation></semantics></math> there.

It passes through <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>7</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-2, -7)</annotation></semantics></math>, with slope <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-4</annotation></semantics></math> there.

items.q: What does <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin^{-1} x</annotation></semantics></math> mean?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>arcsin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\arcsin x</annotation></semantics></math>, the angle in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">[</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]</annotation></semantics></math> whose sine is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\sin x</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\left(x^{-1}\right) = \sin\frac{1}{x}</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: A 13-foot ladder leans against a vertical wall. Its foot is 5 feet from the wall. How high up the wall does the top reach?

mistakes.why: The ladder is the hypotenuse, so subtract: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>13</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^2 = 13^2 - 5^2</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>13</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13^2 + 5^2</annotation></semantics></math>.

The Pythagorean theorem works with squares: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>169</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{169 - 25}</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>13</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13 - 5</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: A conical tank, point down, is 9 feet deep with a top radius of 6 feet. When the water is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> feet deep, its surface has radius <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>. Which equation relates <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>?

For the tank above (<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = \frac{2}{3}h</annotation></semantics></math>), write the volume of water <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> as a function of the depth <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> alone. Use <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Square the whole radius: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\frac{2}{3}h\right)^2 = \frac{4}{9}h^2</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2}{3}h^2</annotation></semantics></math>.

The cone formula has a factor <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{3}\pi \cdot \frac{4}{9}h^2 \cdot h</annotation></semantics></math>.

Replace <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2}{3}h</annotation></semantics></math>, not by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: A person 6 feet tall stands 10 feet from a lamppost 15 feet tall. How long is the person's shadow on the ground?

mistakes.why: The big triangle's base is the whole distance from the post to the shadow's tip, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10 + s</annotation></semantics></math>, not 10: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>6</mn><mi>s</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>15</mn><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{6}{s} = \frac{15}{10 + s}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The shadow is not the distance to the post; set up similar triangles: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>6</mn><mi>s</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>15</mn><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{6}{s} = \frac{15}{10 + s}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Which formula gives the volume of a sphere of radius <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>?
Find the area of a trapezoid with parallel sides 3 and 7 and height 4.

mistakes.why: Average the parallel sides: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3 + 7}{2} \cdot 4</annotation></semantics></math>. Without the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, the area is doubled.

Area is not the product of all three numbers; use <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{b_1 + b_2}{2}h</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find the area of a semicircle with diameter 6.

mistakes.why: The radius is half the diameter: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 3</annotation></semantics></math>, not 6.

That is the whole circle; a semicircle is half: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>9</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{9\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Write the area <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> of an equilateral triangle in terms of its side length <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is a right triangle with legs <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>. An equilateral triangle's height is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}s</annotation></semantics></math>, by the Pythagorean theorem.

Area is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mtext>base</mtext><mo>⋅</mo><mtext>height</mtext><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2} \cdot \text{base} \cdot \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot s \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}s</annotation></semantics></math>; the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> was dropped.

items.q: A box with a square base of side <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> and height <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> has volume 32 cubic inches. Which expresses <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> in terms of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>?
Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 3 and height 5. Give the exact value.

mistakes.why: Square the radius: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>45</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(3)^2(5) = 45\pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi rh</annotation></semantics></math> is the curved surface area; volume is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi r^2 h</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: A balloon rises straight up from a point 50 meters from an observer on level ground. When the balloon is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> meters high, the angle of elevation from the observer is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>. Which equation is true?
